recommendations.rationale: No candidate measurement exists for the adopted holding_tip_speed_weight change: the simulation ran but the evaluation was rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, leaving result, receipt and campaign_comparison null. Until its reach / holding position / holding speed / computation profile and the candidate-minus-baseline comparison are obtained in a phase that budgets evaluation, any further control-parameter change would be based on an untested hypothesis rather than on measurement. No configuration change is proposed or authorized here.

The holding-window co-variation question cannot be answered from what is displayed: only row count and separate error/speed ranges are retained for the six 0.30-0.35 s rows, and no paired per-row table was displayed, even though the sampled backend record is retained. Defer to a phase that displays a derived paired (error, speed) table before drawing any inference about joint variation.

attribution.reason: Within the six sampled holding rows every tip speed (0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s) exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, while the smallest sampled position error (0.007642608585867386 m) is inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest (0.05813810428573256 m) is not, so the failing criterion in that window includes a speed criterion that fails even where position is momentarily inside tolerance. Only six summarized rows and no paired per-row table were displayed, so this remains a bounded, testable characterization rather than a dominant-cause claim; the new feedback adds no paired per-row data.

Documented co-occurrence: mean update duration 17.26331904856488 s against a 0.01 s control period, 35 deadline misses over 35 updates, per-update optimization_solve_s about 15.0-15.7 s at several distinct updates and update_wall_s up to about 29 s. This documents that synchronous update computation exceeds the control period and that every update is flagged as a miss; synchronous wall overruns do not by themselves establish skipped simulated updates, and no causal link to the holding outcome is established.

Recorded outcome characteristic: 34 of 35 updates stopped with User_Requested_Stop and 1 with Solve_Succeeded, converged_updates = 1, and the feasible-return budget is 15.0 s, with cataloged stop reasons budget_best_feasible and relative_seed_improvement. This documents that convergence was rarely reached within the budget; it does not by itself establish an effect on the sampled holding outcome, and per-iteration cost traces are not retained.

The retained first-step comparison covers accepted predicted-versus-measured endpoints at matched next timestamps only (35 aligned pairs; mean tip difference 0.0038032038653228557 m, maximum 0.0076898869753466255 m), which is small relative to the sampled holding errors (up to 0.05813810428573256 m) but is a projected-model endpoint probe over one 0.01 s control step and cannot explain an entire settling failure; no paired per-row holding projection comparison is displayed.

Cataloged optimization_solve_s values of similar magnitude (~15.0-15.7 s) occur at many distinct updates and cataloged update_wall_s values are spread over ~17.9-29.4 s at distinct updates, so the 17.26331904856488 s mean update duration is not an artifact of a single anomalous update.

The one authorized candidate produced no measurement: the simulation receipt completed but the evaluation receipt was rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, and result, receipt and campaign_comparison are null. The hypothesis that a nonzero holding-window tip-speed cost lowers holding-window tip speed therefore remains untested; the baseline measurements supplied with the feedback only restate the failing holding window, the passing terminal reach and the all-miss deadline pattern, so they neither strengthen nor weaken the hypothesis numerically, and no candidate-minus-baseline arithmetic or frozen classification can be stated.

facts.statement: Baseline run cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef, terminal instant (single sample; retained summary): terminal tip position error is 0.007642608585867386 m, inside the 0.01 m settling position limit, and the same value is recorded as the final holding-row error (detail.late_motion[5].error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m). The retained summary records reach_passed = true with reach_tolerance_m = 0.01 m while joint_reach_holding_passed = false, holding_speed_passed = false and sampled_settling_passed = false, so official reach acceptance is distinct from joint reach-plus-holding success. Cataloged late-row error samples also include 0.03407510504995951 m at detail.late_motion[2].error_m. Coverage: one terminal instant plus the six-row final-window summary, not the whole trajectory.

Final sampled holding window (t = 0.30-0.35 s; all six recorded rows, row_count = 6, sample times 0.30/0.31/0.32/0.33/0.34/0.35 s): tip position error spans 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m against the 0.01 m settling position limit, and tip speed spans 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s against the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit. Every one of the six sampled speeds exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, while the smallest sampled position error is inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest is not; sampled_settling_passed = false and holding_speed_passed = false. The window speed maximum (1.5810152739742807 m/s) equals the recorded late_max_speed_m_s. Coverage: these six sampled rows only; not whole-trajectory ranges.

Across the six holding rows only the row count (6) and separate error_m and speed_m_s ranges are retained in this context; no paired per-row (error, speed) table was displayed, so whether sampled holding error and holding speed vary together or independently across those rows is not determinable here. Cataloged per-row error leaves exist for two late rows (0.03407510504995951 m and 0.007642608585867386 m) but no per-row holding-speed leaves were displayed beyond the window minimum/maximum; the underlying sampled backend record is retained but only this window was displayed as a motion view.

Computation (run-level scalars plus per-update leaves present in this catalog): 35 recorded updates at a 0.01 s control period; mean update duration 17.26331904856488 s; deadline_misses = 35 and update_count = 35 (every record flagged as a deadline miss). Cataloged per-update optimization_solve_s values are about 15.0-15.7 s at several distinct updates (e.g. 15.002923699794337, 15.072048399830237, 15.335863699903712, 15.67215109989047, 15.54932660004124, 15.37857409985736 s) and cataloged update_wall_s values are about 17.9-29.4 s (e.g. 17.893660200061277, 17.95735409995541, 18.159177700057626, 18.408669699914753, 29.352235099999234 s); the configured feasible-return budget is 15.0 s and max_iterations is 120. This documents synchronous update wall time far exceeding the control period with each sampled update flagged as a miss; synchronous wall overruns do not by themselves establish skipped simulated updates or any effect on the holding outcome.

Solver and plan-selection records: the retained stopping counts report 1 Solve_Succeeded and 34 User_Requested_Stop, with converged_updates = 1 and accepted plans 35 (6 noninitialization-selected, 29 initialization-selected). Cataloged per-update optimization_raw_status leaves show User_Requested_Stop at several distinct updates (recorded update_ids 7, 9, 11, 30); cataloged policy_stop_reason leaves show budget_best_feasible and relative_seed_improvement; cataloged optimization_selected_iteration leaves read 0 at each update where present (recorded update_ids 0, 3, 8, 11, 20, 26); cataloged plan_accepted leaves read true (recorded update_ids 7, 16, 18, 25, 30). Coverage: run-level stopping/convergence scalars plus only a subset of per-update status, stop-reason, iteration and acceptance leaves.

Cataloged per-update effective_horizon values are 10, 10, 10, 10, 7 and 5 control intervals at a 0.01 s control period (recorded update_ids 7, 9, 10, 24, 28, 30); the remaining updates' effective_horizon leaves are not retained in this catalog, and no legal saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s was identified in the displayed evidence (the retained recipe horizon is 10 intervals). Coverage: a subset of the 35 per-update horizon values, not the full array.

Retained one-step prediction summary: 35 aligned first-step predictions matched to the next execution timestamp, mean tip difference 0.0038032038653228557 m, maximum 0.0076898869753466255 m, none missing. The recorded scope states these compare a projected GVS prediction with a full serial-backend endpoint at the matched next timestamp and applied input, not full state agreement, and that no future-plan replay comparison is made. Cataloged aligned-interval tip differences are small and of similar magnitude (e.g. 0.0015898548075228708, 0.0018617807210030688, 0.0026377648395426068, 0.0033608919551699626 m). Coverage: accepted first-step endpoint comparisons only, over updates 0-34; a one-step projected probe cannot explain an entire settling outcome.

Workflow outcome for the adopted change (decision artifact f4bdcf9020382c34bec9f87f5ca97a63ba54f4d02d9782acf17f6548f3e87b53; candidate 'baseline-replay'; source execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef): the improvement feedback (kind complete_improvement_feedback) reports status = execution_incomplete. The simulation receipt completed with 1 backend solve, but the evaluation receipt was rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (protected downstream capacity; execution_id not_executed), so the candidate result, receipt and campaign_comparison are null and local_screen status is not_requested. No candidate profile number and no candidate-minus-baseline arithmetic or frozen classification therefore exist; the profile block returned with the feedback is labelled baseline facts and matches the baseline execution's terminal, holding and computation records. Coverage: one feedback record for the one authorized candidate; no candidate measurement at all.

Plan-feasibility records: cataloged returned_constraint_violation leaves at distinct recorded update_ids 18, 22, 23, 24 and 29 read 0.010413094332821851, 0.0065736637295124925, 0.0035858652293887464, 0.004741839983090409 and 5.519381696475478e-06, while cataloged selected_constraint_violation leaves are much smaller (e.g. 2.3288662664988635e-11 at update_id 24, 1.197066534439073e-10 at update_id 18, 4.7335377914440105e-06 at update_id 33, 6.5491593623928646e-06 at update_id 32). Coverage: the constraint-violation leaves present in this catalog, not all 35 updates.

limitations: Coverage per area: terminal reach = single terminal instant (retained summary); sampled holding position and sampled holding speed = the six rows of the 0.30-0.35 s window only; computation = run-level scalars plus the per-update solve-time, status and horizon leaves present in this catalog. No trajectory-wide claim is made.

No candidate measurement exists: the adopted change's evaluation was rejected (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, protected downstream capacity), so its profile, campaign comparison and frozen classification are absent and no candidate-minus-baseline arithmetic can be stated. Adoption alone executed nothing further.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability is available; prediction views return projected GVS endpoints over a bounded horizon, not a full backend replay, so no dominant cause is established.
Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent), limiting per-update attribution of solve duration, iteration selection and plan acceptance.

The fact catalog is a compact selection of scalar leaves; per-row values not listed are not asserted. Values not displayed in this context are not the same as never queried: the sampled backend record and the per-update sources were queried, but only a subset of leaves and one motion window are displayed here.

Terminal-instant values are kept distinct from holding-window samples; the numerical coincidence of the terminal error and speed with the window minimum/maximum is an equality in the reported records, not evidence of a causal link.

Any future candidate observation of lower holding speed accompanied by larger position error would be a trade-off, not a criterion pass; official reach-only acceptance and joint reach-plus-holding success are separate flags.
recommended_actions: Advisory (defer): do not make any further control-parameter change on the strength of an unmeasured candidate. The adopted holding_tip_speed_weight change has no profile result (simulation ran, evaluation rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED), so obtain its reach / sampled holding position / sampled holding speed / computation profile and the candidate-minus-baseline comparison under a phase that budgets evaluation before deciding.

Advisory (defer): defer the holding-window co-variation question until a derived paired per-row (error, speed) table over the sampled backend record is displayed; only the six-row final window is displayed as a motion view and the compact catalog carries row count plus separate ranges.

Advisory: when any future candidate is read, keep the official reach-only acceptance separate from joint reach-plus-holding success, and treat lower holding speed with larger position error as a trade-off.
Advisory: no further candidate execution or saved-state check is authorized in this phase, and no configuration change is proposed here.
